f.title: Definition: serious adverse drug reaction (six criteria)
f.statement: Definition (not a stand-alone duty): under these Regulations, a 'serious adverse reaction to drugs' is one where use of a drug results in: (1) death; (2) a life-threatening condition; (3) permanent disability; (4) congenital anomaly/birth defect of a fetus or infant; (5) inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation; or (6) other complications that may result in permanent injury. Reactions meeting any criterion fall within the reporting duty in Article 3(1) (for pharmaceutical firms, the 15-day time limit in Article 7).
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firms, medical care institutions and pharmacies (in applying the reporting duty)
rows.review_note: Review: a definition, not an obligation. Title and statement are reworded as a definition that sets the scope of the Article 3/7 reporting duty. Level kept Mandatory because GUIDE.md says definitions that change what must be reported take Mandatory when the instrument makes them binding (this is a binding regulation). The double-check should confirm this reading of the guide. Double-check: Mandatory accepted: GUIDE records definitions that change what must be reported as Mandatory when the instrument makes them binding, and this Article 2 definition in a binding regulation sets the scope of the Article 3 reporting duty. Statement corrected: the 15-day limit applies to pharmaceutical firms only (institutions and pharmacies have 7/30 days under Article 6). Definition row, not a stand-alone duty; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE. Deletion of former -0015 (Article 13 implementation date) confirmed correct: it is an effective-date provision with no duty, already carried in every row applicability.

f.title: Report serious adverse drug reactions via the designated online system
f.statement: Pharmaceutical firms holding a drug manufacturing or importing approval (as well as medical care institutions and pharmacies) shall report each serious adverse drug reaction (Article 2) to the central competent health authority's designated online system by filling out a report form once they become aware of it. Firms must complete this within 15 days of awareness (Article 7).
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.deadline: Within 15 days from the awareness date (Article 7)
rows.quote: Medical care institutions, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical firms that have obtained a drug manufacturing or importing approval (hereinafter referred to as “pharmaceutical firms”) shall report to the central competent health authority's designated online system by filling out a report form upon becoming aware of a serious adverse reaction to a drug as described in the previous article.
rows.review_note: Review: added the cross-reference to the 15-day time limit (Article 7) in the statement and deadline. The translation's parenthesis defines 'pharmaceutical firms' as those with a manufacturing or import approval, which the actor already reflects. Double-check: quote proves the online reporting duty and actor; the 15-day limit comes from Article 7 (separate row -0008), not this quote; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Preliminary reports may be oral, phone, fax or email, but online report still due on time
f.statement: Reports may be made orally, by telephone, fax or email as necessary; however, the online report must still be completed within the time limits in Articles 6 or 7.
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).
f.exceptions: Online reporting remains mandatory within the Article 6/7 time limits.

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.quote: Reporting under the previous paragraph may be made orally, by telephone, fax, or email as necessary. However, online reporting must be completed within the time limits specified in Articles 6 or 7.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Permitted level covers the optional oral/phone/fax/email preliminary report; the mandatory online completion is kept as a condition. Double-check: Permitted for the optional preliminary channels with the mandatory online completion kept as a condition; mixed level within one quote; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Correct unclear or incomplete serious ADR reports within the time limit when ordered
f.statement: If the central competent health authority considers a serious ADR report (online or preliminary) unclear or incomplete, it may order the reporter to correct it within a specified time limit; the reporting pharmaceutical firm shall make the corrections within that time limit.
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).
f.exceptions: Applies only when the authority issues a correction order (authority discretion: 'may').

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (reporter), when ordered by the central competent health authority
rows.deadline: Within the time limit specified by the authority
rows.quote: If the central competent health authority deems the report content submitted under the preceding 2 paragraphs unclear or incomplete, it may order the reporter to make corrections within a specified time limit.
rows.review_note: Review: level Permitted -> Mandatory. The 'may' is the authority's discretion to order corrections; the reporter's duty is to comply once ordered (same treatment as TW PAA Article 48 and DSS Articles 7 and 9). Statement and actor restated. Double-check: Mandatory accepted as a judgement call: statement is framed as the reporter duty to correct once ordered, but the quote only gives the authority power to order corrections and states no sanction; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Report form may follow the ICH electronic transmission format
f.statement: The report form may be filled out according to the ICH electronic transmission standardization format.
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.quote: The reporting form referred to in the previous article may be filled out according to the electronic transmission standardization format of the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Permitted level matches "may"; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Include the required content in serious ADR reports
f.statement: Reports under Article 3 contain: reporter name, contact information and service unit name and address; occurrence and awareness dates of the serious adverse drug reaction; source of information; patient identification code, gender, and age or date of birth; patient medication information; and category, symptoms and description of the serious adverse drug reaction.
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.quote:
Content of Reports under Article 3
1. Reporter's name, contact information, and the name and address of their service unit.
2. Occurrence and awareness dates of the serious adverse drug reaction.
3. Source of information about the serious adverse drug reaction.
4. Patient identification code, gender, and age or date of birth.
5. Patient medication information.
6. Category, symptoms, and related description of the serious adverse drug reaction.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Article 5 is a heading plus list with no modal verb, so Mandatory is a judgement call and the content is list-derived; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Provide product information to institutions and pharmacies reporting serious ADRs
f.statement: Medical care institutions and pharmacies may request pharmaceutical firms to provide product-related information for their serious ADR reports; pharmaceutical firms shall not evade, obstruct or refuse to provide such information.
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).
f.processes: Local PV interfaces; Safety intake & collection

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.quote: Medical care institutions and pharmacies may request pharmaceutical firms to provide product-related information for reporting under the preceding paragraph. The pharmaceutical firms shall not evade, obstruct, or refuse to provide such information.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves the firm prohibition on refusing product information; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Complete serious ADR reports within 15 days of awareness
f.statement: Pharmaceutical firms shall complete serious adverse drug reaction reports under Article 3(1) within 15 days from the awareness date of the reporting matter.
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.deadline: Within 15 days from the awareness date
rows.quote: Pharmaceutical firms shall complete reports under Paragraph 1 of Article 3 within 15 days from the reporting matter's awareness date.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Clock: 15 days from the awareness date. For medical institutions and pharmacies, Article 6 counts 7 or 30 days from the day following awareness; those duties are not captured as company duties. Double-check: quote proves actor, 15-day limit and clock start (awareness date); English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Report new or follow-up information on cases forwarded by the authority
f.statement: The central competent health authority may forward serious ADR reports from medical care institutions and pharmacies to pharmaceutical firms. Pharmaceutical firms that receive such forwarded reports and have new, updated or supplementary information shall report it under Article 3(1)-(2) and Article 7 (15 days).
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Submission operations; Reconciliation

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.quote:
The central competent health authority may forward relevant reporting information to pharmaceutical firms upon receiving a serious adverse drug reaction report from medical care institutions and pharmacies.
Pharmaceutical firms that receive such forwarding from the central competent health authority and have new, updated, or supplementary reporting information shall comply with the provisions of Paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 3, and the preceding article regarding reporting.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: duty is by cross-reference to Article 3(1)-(2) and Article 7, so the 15-day limit is inferred from those Articles; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Investigate and assess causality of serious adverse drug reactions
f.statement: Upon becoming aware of a serious adverse drug reaction, pharmaceutical firms shall proactively investigate and assess the causal relationship associated with the reported information.
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.quote: Upon becoming aware of a serious adverse drug reaction, pharmaceutical firms shall proactively investigate and assess the causal relationship associated with the reported information.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves actor and duty; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Escalate unexpected or higher-frequency serious ADRs under the safety surveillance rules
f.statement: If the investigation and assessment reveals a serious adverse drug reaction occurring at an unexpected or higher-than-expected frequency, or a need to add or change contraindications or usage restrictions, the matter shall be handled under Article 6 of the Regulations for the Management of Drug Safety Surveillance.
f.legal_basis: Regulations for the Management of Drug Safety Surveillance Art 6
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).
f.processes: Signal management; Submission operations; Safety labeling

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.quote: If pharmaceutical firms discover a serious adverse drug reaction that occurs at an unexpected or higher-than-expected frequency or if it is necessary to add or change contraindications or usage restrictions based on the investigation and assessment results under the preceding paragraph, the matter shall be handled according to Article 6 of the Regulations for the Management of Drug Safety Surveillance.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: passive "the matter shall be handled" defers the substance to DSS Article 6; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Retain serious ADR records until 5 years after approval expiry
f.statement: Pharmaceutical firms shall retain documents and data related to serious adverse drug reactions until 5 years after the drug manufacturing or importing approval expires (medical care institutions and pharmacies: at least 5 years).
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.deadline: Until 5 years after the manufacturing or importing approval expires
rows.quote:
Medical care institutions, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical firms shall retain relevant documents and data related to serious adverse drug reactions for the following periods:
1. Medical care institutions and pharmacies: At least 5 years.
2. Pharmaceutical firms: Until 5 years after the drug manufacturing or importing approval expires.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves the firm retention period; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Provide serious ADR records on request; do not evade or refuse
f.statement: The central competent health authority may request the retained serious ADR documents and data; pharmaceutical firms shall not evade, obstruct or refuse to provide them.
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.quote: The central competent health authority may request medical care institutions, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical firms to provide the documents and data specified in the preceding paragraph. Medical care institutions, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical firms shall not evade, obstruct, or refuse to provide such information.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves the prohibition; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Comply with the Personal Data Protection Act when handling ADR personal data
f.statement: Pharmaceutical firms shall comply with the Personal Data Protection Act and related regulations when collecting, processing or using personal data under these Regulations.
f.applicability: Taiwan; English translation published by TFDA (Chinese text prevails). The amended Regulations (amended 28 March 2024) apply from 1 January 2025 (Article 13).

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (drug manufacturing or import approval holder)
rows.quote: Medical care institutions, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical firms shall comply with the Personal Data Protection Act and its related regulations when collecting, processing, or utilizing personal data according to the Regulations.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves actor and duty; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.
